'''Jean-Paul Pier''' (July 5, 1933 – December 14, 2016) was a [[Luxembourg]]ish mathematician, specializing in [[harmonic analysis]] and the [[history of mathematics]], particularly mathematical analysis in the 20th century.

==Education and career==
Jean-Paul Pier was a graduate student in Luxembourg and at the universities of Paris and Nancy. He earned a [[University of Luxembourg]] doctorate in [[mathematical sciences]] and a French doctorate in [[pure mathematics]]. He also spent six months at the [[Grenoble]] Nuclear Research Center (1961) and a year at the [[University of Oregon]] (1966-1967).

He taught mathematics at the [[Lycée de Garçons de Luxembourg|Lycée de Garçons]] in [[Esch-sur-Alzette]] from 1956 to 1980. In 1971 he created the ''Séminaire de mathématiques''<ref>[http://wwwfr.uni.lu/recherche/fstc/mathematics_research_unit/colloquium_and_seminars/general_mathematics_seminar Séminaire de mathématiques de l'université du Luxembourg]</ref> at the Centre universitaire de Luxembourg (now the [[University of Luxembourg]]). He was a professor at the Centre from its creation in 1974 until 1998, when he retired as [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Luxembourg Mathematical Society|website=MacTutor History of Mathematics|url=http://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Societies/Luxembourg.html}}</ref>

Pier was primarily responsible for the creation in January 1989 of the [[Luxembourg Mathematical Society]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Luxembourg Mathematical Society (about us)|website=math.uni.lu|url=http://math.uni.lu/sml/}}</ref> of which he was president from 1989 to 1993 and again from 1995 to 1998. He was during the academic year 1994–1995 a visiting professor at the [[Université catholique de Louvain]].

Pier was the editor of two scholarly anthologies, which are standard works on the history of 20th-century mathematics. He organized several [[Seminar|colloquia]] and conferences in Luxembourg. He was active internationally in various scientific bodies, including [[NATO Science for Peace and Security]] and [[UNESCO]].

==Selected publications==
* ''Amenable locally compact groups'', Wiley, 1984.
* ''Amenable Banach algebras'', Longman, 1988.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1990-15865-3|title=Book Review: ''Amenable Banach algebras''|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=22|pages=145–149|year=1990|last1=Sinclair|first1=Allan M.|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* ''L'Analyse harmonique. Son développement historique'', Masson, 1990.
* ''Histoire de l'intégration, vingt-cinq siècles de mathématiques'', Masson, 1996.
* ''Mathematical Analysis during the 20th century'', Oxford University Press, 2001<ref name="Abbott2016">{{cite journal|last1=Abbott|first1=Steve|title=Review of ''Mathematical analysis during the 20th century'', by Jean-Paul Pier|journal=The Mathematical Gazette|volume=87|issue=509|year=2003|pages=392–393|issn=0025-5572|doi=10.1017/S0025557200173334|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* ''Mathématiques entre savoir et connaissance'', Vuibert, 2006.
* ''Development of Mathematics 1900-1950'', edited by Jean-Paul Pier, Birkhäuser, 1994.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Gray, Jeremy|author-link=Jeremy Gray (mathematician)|title=Review of ''Development of Mathematics, 1900–1950'' edited by Jean-Paul Pier|journal=Historia Mathematica|volume=23|issue=4|year=1996|pages=437–440|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82169858.pdf|doi=10.1006/hmat.1996.0041|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=rB7BjYsD2j4C Development of Mathematics 1950-2000]'', edited by Jean-Paul Pier, Birkhäuser, 2000.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.2307/3622059|jstor=3622059|title=Review of ''Development of Mathematics 1950-2000''|journal=The Mathematical Gazette|volume=85|issue=503|pages=356|year=2001|last1=Abbott|first1=Steve}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Mazzotti, Massimo|title=Review of ''Development of Mathematics 1950-2000''|journal=British Journal for the History of Science|volume=35|issue=125|year=2002|pages=245–246|url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/48564330ddda7988d10583ae8af1b6c7/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=7133}}</ref>
* ''Gabriel Lippmann. Commémoration par la section des sciences naturelles, physiques et mathématiques de l’Institut grand-ducal de Luxembourg du 150<sup>e</sup> anniversaire du savant né au Luxembourg lauréat du prix Nobel en 1908'', J.-P. Pier et J. A. Massard, éditeurs, 1997.
* ''Le Choix de la parole'', Lethielleux/DDB, 2009.
